checklist.item: Visit https://hackenproof.com/programs/tetu-smart-contracts and extract exact in-scope contracts, excluded contracts, severity tiers, and submission formatting rules.
Clone the official TETU Git repository referenced on the program page and note commit hash used for mainnet deployments.
Run agents/deep_dive_audit.py on the cloned repo, pointing it at the core vaults, strategies, controller, and reward distributor contracts on Polygon.
Execute the full static suite (Slither + Aderyn + Mythril) inside deep_dive_audit.py and triage all high/critical findings for access-control or reentrancy patterns.
Trigger Halmos symbolic execution via the same script on fee accrual, reward distribution, and strategy migration functions to search for under-constrained states.
Manually review oracle usage, proxy upgrade paths, and cross-contract calls against the real deployment addresses for business-logic and trust issues.
Check for common EVM pitfalls (unchecked return values, incorrect msg.value handling, storage collisions) not covered by automated tools.
Prepare submission package containing PoC, exact contract addresses, reproduction transaction hashes, and severity justification that matches Hackenproof template.
Submit the report through the Hackenproof platform only after confirming the finding is not already disclosed or out of scope.
Verify the current scope, rules, and payout tiers for the TETU Smart Contracts bug bounty program directly on the Hackenproof website to ensure accuracy and avoid any potential misunderstandings.
Identify the specific smart contracts and repositories included in the scope, focusing on those written in Solidity for Ethereum and Polygon.
Clone or download the relevant Solidity contracts from the specified git repository to prepare them for analysis.

Run agents/deep_dive_audit.py on the cloned Solidity contracts to perform a comprehensive analysis using Slither, Halmos symbolic execution, Mythril, Aderyn static AST analysis, and frontier-LLM review.
Manually review the analysis results against a real vulnerability taxonomy, checking for issues such as access control, oracle trust, reentrancy, and business logic vulnerabilities.
Investigate any potential vulnerabilities identified during the analysis, verifying their exploitability and impact on the contracts.
Document all findings, including steps to reproduce, exploit code (if applicable), and recommendations for remediation, to prepare a comprehensive submission.
Ensure the submission meets all the requirements outlined in the program's rules and guidelines, including formatting and content expectations.
Submit the findings through the Hackenproof platform, following the specified procedure for the TETU Smart Contracts bug bounty program.
